productName: Executive Care Pro Critical Illness Insurance Plan 2

trends.whatProductOffers: Covers 61 critical illnesses made up of 53 major illnesses, 2 minor illnesses, 1 early stage critical illness, 4 severe child diseases and female carcinoma-in-situ, with protection up to age 100.

keyFigures.label: Critical illnesses covered
keyFigures.condition: 53 major, 2 minor, 1 early stage, 4 severe child diseases, female carcinoma-in-situ

exclusionsOrConditions: Total claims other than the male cancer extra benefit cannot exceed 100% of the Initial Sum Assured, excluding Terminal Dividend.
Advance payments reduce the Current Sum Assured, premium, guaranteed cash value and future dividends.
The covered illness schedule and definitions are in the policy contract.
clientProfileFit: Parents wanting child disease cover alongside adult CI
trends.talkingPointTemplate: For {client_detail}, 61 conditions are covered from early stage through major illness, up to age 100.
verificationPrompts: Confirm the 61-illness schedule and the definition of each category.
Confirm the claim limits across categories.
Confirm the severe child disease definitions and age limits.
sourceEvidence: Executive Care Pro Critical Illness Insurance Plan 2 provides you with critical illness protections up to the age of 100. It covers 53 major illnesses, 2 minor illnesses, 1 early stage critical illness, 4 severe child diseases and female Carcinoma-in-situ.
trends.notesForReviewer: Illness definitions and claim percentages per category are not in the extracted text.

trends.whatProductOffers: Pays an extra 10% of the major illness benefit amount if the insured is diagnosed with testicular or prostate cancer after his 18th birthday, on top of the major illness benefit.

keyFigures.label: Extra payment
keyFigures.condition: testicular or prostate cancer after age 18

exclusionsOrConditions: Applies only to male insureds and only to testicular and prostate cancer.
The extra benefit is paid in addition to the major illness benefit and sits outside the 100% Initial Sum Assured cap.
Diagnosis must occur after the insured's 18th birthday.
clientSignalPhrases: male client, family history of prostate cancer
negativeSignalPhrases: wants extra cover for other cancers
clientProfileFit: Male clients with family history of prostate cancer
trends.talkingPointTemplate: For a male client like {client_detail}, a prostate or testicular cancer diagnosis pays an extra 10% on top of the major illness benefit.
verificationPrompts: Confirm the male cancer benefit definition and whether it applies to early stage diagnoses.
Confirm the benefit is outside the 100% Initial Sum Assured cap.
sourceEvidence: If the insured is diagnosed with male cancer (i.e. testicular and prostate cancer) after his 18th birthday, in addition to the benefit for major illness, we will pay an extra 10% of benefit amount paid under major illness.

trends.whatProductOffers: A participating plan that accumulates wealth through guaranteed cash value, non-guaranteed Annual Dividends credited each policy year, and a one-off non-guaranteed Terminal Dividend once the policy has been in force for 10 years.
exclusionsOrConditions: Annual and Terminal Dividends are non-guaranteed and may be lower than illustrated, including zero.
The Terminal Dividend requires the policy to have been in force for 10 years.
Advance illness payments reduce cash value and future dividends.
clientSignalPhrases: doesn't want money wasted if no claim
clientProfileFit: Clients building retirement assets alongside protection
trends.talkingPointTemplate: {client_detail} builds guaranteed cash value plus annual dividends, with a terminal dividend after ten years.
verificationPrompts: Request the benefit illustration with guaranteed and non-guaranteed values.
Confirm the current dividend history and bonus philosophy.
sourceEvidence: Executive Care Pro Critical Illness Insurance Plan 2 offers guaranteed cash value and non-guaranteed Annual Dividends.
a one-off non-guaranteed cash amount, called a Terminal Dividend, provided that the policy has been in force for 10 years.
trends.notesForReviewer: No illustrated values or dividend rates in the extracted text.

trends.whatProductOffers: Waives subsequent premiums on the basic policy after a major illness claim, while attached add-on plans remain in force if their own premiums continue to be paid.

keyFigures.label: Add-on plans
keyFigures.condition: if their premiums continue to be paid

exclusionsOrConditions: The waiver applies to the basic policy only, not to add-on premiums.
Add-on plans continue only while their premiums are paid.
The waiver is triggered by a major illness claim, not a minor illness or early stage claim.
clientSignalPhrases: worried about paying premium after diagnosis
wants cover to continue after claim
wants no more premiums if seriously ill
negativeSignalPhrases: expects premiums waived after any claim
clientProfileFit: Clients worried about premium affordability after diagnosis
trends.talkingPointTemplate: After a major illness claim, {client_detail} stops paying premiums on the basic plan while the cover stays in force.
verificationPrompts: Confirm which claim categories trigger the waiver.
Confirm the treatment of add-on premiums after the waiver.
sourceEvidence: In case of any major illness claims made, the subsequent premium of the basic policy will be waived. Add-on plans (if any) attached to the basic policy will remain in force and provide cover if their respective premiums continue to be paid.
trends.notesForReviewer: Waiver is on the basic policy only.

trends.whatProductOffers: Pays a death benefit comprising the Current Sum Assured, accumulated Annual Dividends with interest, and a one-off Terminal Dividend if the policy has been in force for 10 years; the plan also covers 4 severe child diseases.

keyFigures.label: Death benefit components
keyFigures.condition: Current Sum Assured + accumulated Annual Dividends + Terminal Dividend

exclusionsOrConditions: Outstanding debt under the policy is deducted before payment.
Terminal Dividend applies only if the policy has been in force for 10 years.
Death benefit is reduced by any advance payments already made.
negativeSignalPhrases: needs a large standalone term cover

trends.talkingPointTemplate: {client_detail}'s family receives the sum assured plus accumulated dividends and any terminal dividend on death.
